requirements.text: Reassign change request 'CHG0000017' (Monthly Firewall Rule Audit) to 'steven.hernandez88@servicenow.com'
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM change WHERE change_id = 'CHG_017' AND assigned_to = 'USER_009'
assumptions: CHG0000017 resolved to CHG_017 by number; its short_description matches 'Monthly Firewall Rule Audit'; seed assignee is USER_045
steven.hernandez88@servicenow.com resolved to USER_009 (agent, active, ORG_001), who satisfies policy 8.1's active-user rule for assignment
the benchmark check's number = CHG0000017 and org_id = ORG_001 are the row's existing identity, covered by the anchor and unchanged by a reassignment
USER_009 is in GROUP_002, not the change's assignment_group GROUP_007; policy 3.2's group rule is for incidents and the request names him outright, so assignment_group is not tested

requirements.text: map this change to problem 'PRB0000006' as the root cause resolution
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM change_request_mapping WHERE change_id = 'CHG_017' AND problem_id = 'PRB_006' AND org_id = 'ORG_001'
assumptions: PRB0000006 resolved to PRB_006 by number
selected by natural key (change and problem), not by sequence id: the task creates two mapping rows and fixes no order
'check if they already exist': no mapping for CHG_017 exists on the seed (the PRB_006 and INC_025 mappings there, CRM_012 and CRM_004, belong to CHG_005), so the row must be created

org_id = ORG_001 kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy, but it is the change's and the acting user's org and the seed's existing mapping to PRB_006 uses it, although PRB_006 itself is ORG_017
'as the root cause resolution' has no column in the mapping table; not tested

disagreement: form: A repeats the natural key (change_id, problem_id) and org_id in the selector and in cells, B puts the natural key in the selector and org_id alone in cells; kept B's because cells hold only what the requirement tests beyond its selector; the sql is identical

requirements.text: link it to incident 'INC-000025' to establish complete traceability
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM change_request_mapping WHERE change_id = 'CHG_017' AND incident_id = 'INC_025' AND org_id = 'ORG_001'
assumptions: INC-000025 resolved to INC_025 by number
selected by natural key (change and incident), not by sequence id, for the same reason as the problem mapping
org_id = ORG_001 kept from the benchmark check; the incident row itself is ORG_015 on the seed, but the change and the existing CHG_005 mapping to it (CRM_004) are ORG_001
the link is the mapping row only: no tool here writes incident.change_request, and the request names mappings
disagreement: form: as for the problem mapping (A repeats the natural key in cells, B does not); kept B's; the sql is identical

requirements.text: Verify all change request mappings for this change to ensure proper documentation of the problem-change-incident relationship
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM change_request_mapping WHERE change_id = 'CHG_017' AND org_id = 'ORG_001' AND (problem_id = 'PRB_006' OR incident_id = 'INC_025')
assumptions: the two links are two mapping rows, one per target, as every seed mapping carries either a problem or an incident, never both; the schema's CHECK would admit one row carrying both ids, which the two single-row requirements would pass and this count of two fails

exactly two also rules out duplicate mappings, which the 'check if they already exist' step is meant to prevent (the table's unique constraints on org, change and target block exact duplicates anyway)
disagreement: form: A carries change_id and org_id in cells and org_id in the selector, B org_id alone in cells; kept B's; the sql is identical

requirements.text: Before creating any mappings, check if they already exist (boundary: the existing mappings of another change to the same problem and incident)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM change_request_mapping WHERE change_request_mapping_id IN ('CRM_004', 'CRM_012') AND change_id = 'CHG_005'
assumptions: CRM_004 (CHG_005 -> INC_025) and CRM_012 (CHG_005 -> PRB_006) are what a loose 'already exist' lookup by problem or incident would find; they belong to CHG_005 and must not be repointed to CHG_017

disagreement: selector form: A names the two rows with change_id = CHG_005 as the cell, B selects change_id = CHG_005 AND (problem_id = PRB_006 OR incident_id = INC_025) with no cells; both count 2 on the seed and both fail if either row is repointed or removed; kept A's because it names the rows the boundary protects and keeps the tested column in cells

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the four benchmark checks (all kept), the reassignment of CHG_017 to USER_009, the two mapping rows selected by natural key with org_id ORG_001, the chain check carried as a count of two, and the stay on CHG_005's existing mappings CRM_004 and CRM_012; the passes differ only in form, with identical sql throughout.
disagreement: form of the three mapping requirements: A repeats the natural-key columns (and org_id) in both selector and cells, B keeps the natural key in the selector and org_id alone in cells; kept B's because cells hold only what the requirement tests beyond its selector (logged on each requirement).
disagreement: form of the CHG_005 stay: A names the two rows with change_id as the cell, B selects by change and target with no cells; kept A's, which names the rows the boundary protects (logged on the requirement).
The chain check is not carried jointly by the two single-row mappings but kept as its own count-of-two requirement, as both passes had it, because it tests something the single-row requirements do not: the links are separate rows (the schema's CHECK admits a row with both ids) and there are no duplicates. The problem (ORG_017) and incident (ORG_015) belong to other organisations than the change (ORG_001); the benchmark fixes the mapping org_id to ORG_001 and the seed's existing mappings of the same two records to CHG_005 do the same, so that value is kept rather than treated as a contradiction. The 'verify all mappings' sentence is a read step with no further state of its own.
